newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oriental Land up sharply after media report.
newsitem.headline: Oriental Land up sharply after media report.

text.p: Shares in Oriental Land Co Ltd, which operates Tokyo Disneyland, rose sharply in early afternoon trade after a media report that the company would decide at a board meeting on Tuesday to provide tickets to its facilities to shareholders.
By 0425 GMT, Oriental Land shares were up 310 yen at 8,100. Turnover was about 160,000 shares.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported in its evening edition on Tuesday that Oriental Land planned to provide entrance and ride tickets to Tokyo Disneyland to each shareholder who has at least 100 shares in the company.
The paper also said that the company might pay an annual dividend larger than its previous forecast.
The company has said it would pay a 10 yen annual dividend for the year to March 31, up two yen from a year ago, but it may increase that to 11 to 12 yen, the paper said.
An Oriental Land spokesman told Reuters that the company had made no announcements on the issues.
He confirmed there would be a board meeting on Tuesday afternoon, but he declined to say whether these issues would be discussed.
